content.text:
This figure is from AC 43.13-1B, Acceptable Methods, Techniques, and Practices: Aircraft Inspection and Repair, chapter 7 (aircraft hardware, control cables, and turnbuckles). Its caption: "FIGURE 7-12. Typical cable splices.".
Describe it for a mechanic who can't see it: say what it shows, then transcribe every label,
value, unit, part number, and note printed in it. Don't add anything that isn't in the figure.
If it shows nothing of use (a logo, a signature, a blank area), say so in one sentence.

message.content:
The figure shows three typical aircraft control cable splice configurations labeled (a), (b), and (c), each illustrating different hardware arrangements for joining or terminating cable ends.

Labels, values, units, part numbers, and notes printed in the figure:

(a)
- AN 668 TERMINAL
- CLEVIS BOLT
- AN 667
- AN 320 SHEAR NUT AND COTTER PIN

(b)
- 1/8" OR MORE
- 1/2" OR MORE
- TURNBUCKLE ASSEMBLY
- Numbers 1, 2, 3 (appearing twice, once on each side of the turnbuckle)

(c)
- CLEVIS BOLT
- AN 111 BUSHING
- AN 320 SHEAR NUT AND COTTER PIN
